newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power jumps with gas, BPA caps rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power jumps with gas, BPA caps rise.

text.p: Western U.S. spot electricity prices in the western U.S. surged with natural gas Monday due to low temperatures forecast for the region this week.
Some market sources said Bonneville Power Administration's (BPA) resumption to offer firm, next-day power during heavy load hours today capped the rise in the daily market.
"BPA undercut everyone else today," a Houston marketer said. Marketers and other participants usually try to undersell the federal marketing agency.
In early trading, electricity for Tuesday's peak hours in the Northwest was running at least a dollar a megawatt hour above BPA's daily posted prices for pre-scheduled power.
BPA offered next-day power for firm, peak delivery at $26.00/MWh at the California-Oregon Border (COB), and $16.00 for firm, off-peak delivery.
Swing gas prices at San Juan/Blanco Hub in New Mexico were quoted at $4.05-$4.10 per million British thermal units.
"Power (prices) should have gone higher, but there's a lot more hydro coming down in January," said a Houston broker.

There remained concerns over the amount of hydroelectric output this spring after recent weeks of heavy rain in the Pacific Northwest and signs of early snowpack in the region's mountainous, the broker said.
Firm, peak COB electricity for Tuesday was assessed at $26.00-$28.00/MWh, sharply higher than Friday's $23.00-$24.00.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Tuesday was quoted near $16.00, compared with a range of $15.50-17.00 Friday.
First-quarter 1997 COB power was quoted at $22.75-$23.25 and second-quarter COB near $15.25.
Tuesday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was pegged at $27.00-$29.00, much higher than $21.00-22.00 Friday. Off-peak Mid-C was talked near $16.00-$17.25, up from Friday's $15.00-16.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Tuesday was quoted $27.00-$29.00, significantly higher than Friday's $22.00-23.00.
Off-peak PV for firm delivery Tuesday was quoted near $15.00-$16.00, up from $13.50-15.00 Friday.
First-quarter 1997 PV electricity was quoted at $23.50-$24.35 and second-quarter PV at $18.00-$18.50.
Tuesday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were higher in tandem with much stronger PV prices, notationally assessed at $27.50-$29.50, up from $22.00-23.00 Friday.
Firm, off-peak Four Corners power was assessed at $15.50-$16.50, much higher than Friday's $13.50-14.50.
